summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, and coronary artery disease was admitted for worsening thoracic back pain and hypoxemia. She had run out of her tramadol, leading to poorly controlled pain, and developed shortness of breath. Imaging showed stable spinal fractures with no acute abdominal findings. Hypoxia initially noted during ambulation was determined to be due to artifactual readings from finger probe interference; when reassessed with an earlobe probe, oxygen saturation was normal. Chronic interstitial lung markings were noted on chest X-ray, but no infection or acute cardiopulmonary process was found. An echocardiogram incidentally revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% with mild-to-moderate systolic dysfunction, which was asymptomatic and to be managed outpatient. Vitamin D was restarted for osteoporosis, and she was discharged home with services after pain control and clinical stability were achieved.
